subject: Physics
topic: Position needs an origin and a direction
title: Position Needs an Origin and a Direction
summary: "200 m" means nothing until you say from where and which way. Position is a signed number with a unit, measured from a chosen origin.

notes.title: Position Needs an Origin and a Direction

keyPoints: To give a position, first choose a reference point, the **origin (O)**.
Choose one direction as **positive**; positions on the other side are **negative**.
Position = **sign + number + unit**, e.g. shop +200 m, school −150 m.
Changing the origin changes every position, but **not the displacement** (final − initial position).

list: Pick the origin and the positive direction, and state them.
A negative position means "on the other side of the origin", not "less than nothing".
Positions depend on the origin; displacements and distances do not.

quiz.q: Your home is the origin and right is positive. A shop 200 m to the left is at:
quiz.explain: Left of the origin is the negative direction.

quiz.q: What must you choose before writing a position?
options: An origin and a positive direction
quiz.explain: Position is measured from an origin along a chosen direction.

quiz.q: If the origin is moved, the positions of objects:
quiz.explain: Each position is measured from the new origin.

quiz.q: Home is at +150 m and the shop at +350 m (school as origin). The displacement home → shop is:
quiz.explain: 350 − 150 = +200 m, the same as with home as origin.

simulation.reason: What depends on the origin and what does not is a hypothesis to test: dragging the origin to any point and flipping the positive direction shows every position change while the displacement stays fixed (and only its sign flips with the direction). A fixed example shows this for one or two origins, not any origin.
simulation.objective: Move the origin and flip the direction, and find which numbers change and which stay the same.
instructions: Predict what will change, then drag the red flag along the road.
Put the origin at School and compare the table with the notes.
Press Flip positive direction and compare the signs and sizes.
